title: subpoena witness line
description: One line of witness output: one exec as the kernel saw it, one send from a session cgroup, one file change under a watched root, one statement a database witness saw, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record, one with a file_op field a file change, one with a delivery_op field a send, one with an event field a row line, and any other line an exec. See docs/ports.md (W, W7, W8, W9). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the exec, send or file change was seen (for a send or file change, when the witness read it), when a statement's outcome became known, or when the record was written (RFC 3339, UTC).

pid.description: PID in the process's own PID namespace.

ppid.description: Parent PID in the process's own PID namespace.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

exe.description: The path passed to execve; may be relative.

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for execs and sends inside a session cgroup, and absent on a file change from a tier-1 witness, which belongs to every trace.

attribution.description: How the line was tied to a trace. cgroup: present exactly when trace_id is. root: a file change seen under a watched root, returned for every trace. destination: a row line, which holds for every trace.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.

path.description: The absolute path changed, spelled from the root as it was given.

root.description: The watched root path is under.

source.description: inotify: the kernel queued the event. scan: a scan of a new directory found the entry; file_op is create whatever was done to it. stat: no event named the path, but the check at stop found it differing from the start, which a chmod does too.

rename.description: Which side of a rename path is.

cookie.description: Ties the two sides of a rename; absent when zero.

roots.description: On a file witness's start record: the directories it watched.

captures.description: On a start record: the hooks that ran. exec: the process witness. delivery: the send hook. A file that does not list delivery cannot pass a no-delivery check.

coverage.description: On a stop record: what the capture might have missed even when healthy, in one line.

silent_closes.description: On a file witness's stop record: files opened for writing and closed with no write seen. No absence rests on them.

symlinks.description: On a file witness's stop record: the symlinks under the roots. A path crossing one is not covered.

delivery_op.description: deliver: a send on a connected socket, to the peer the socket holds. sendmsg: a send that named its destination.

protocol.description: tcp, udp, or another IP protocol name or number.

peer.description: The far end of the send as address:port ([address]:port for IPv6). Empty when the witness could not read it: such a send may have gone to any peer.

local.description: This end of the socket, in the same form; empty when unknown.

bytes.description: Bytes the caller asked to send, not bytes the peer received.

event.description: Row lines only: the kind of event.

conn.description: The witness's number for the connection, from 1.

dest.description: The address the application connected to.

statement.description: SQL text as sent, cut at 8 KiB; empty when none was seen. Never bound values.

tables.description: Tables written, as named, with quotes removed and unquoted parts lower case. A reader must treat an empty list on a write as every table.

opaque.description: The witness could not tell what the statement writes: it counts against every table.

rows.description: Rows the server said it changed, or -1 if its reply gave no usable count. Zero is no effect; a line without this field is an error.

outcome.description: read: writes nothing. committed: the server committed it. rolled_back and failed: not an effect. unknown: its fate was not seen, and the file is a capture fault.
